beliefs: f maps every lowercase letter to the next uppercase letter in ASCII: a→B, m→N, z→{ [E1, E2, E3, E4]
f maps every uppercase letter to the next uppercase letter in ASCII: A→B, M→N, Z→[ [E1, E2, E3, E4]
f maps digits and punctuation by raw ASCII +1: 0→1, 9→:, space→!, @→A, `→a [E1, E2, E3, E4]
There is no case preservation and no wrapping: the shift is simply ord(ch)+1 for every character [E1, E2, E3, E4]
notes: All evidence is consistent with raw ASCII +1 on every character; my earlier v3 mistakenly tried case-preserving Caesar shifts. Reverted to the simple uniform ord+1 rule.
